title: WPSS/1753/2023 of VIKRAM NEGI Vs UTTARAKHAND PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No.1753 of 2023
Vikram Negi ........Petitioner

Present:-
Mr. Sandeep Tiwari, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned counsel for respondent no.1-
Commission.
Mr. Bhupendra Koranga, learned Brief Holder for the State/
respondent nos.2 & 3.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)

By means of this writ petition, petitioner has
challenged the result dated 06.07.2023, annexure-7 to
the writ petition issued by Commission only with respect
to the selection of the respondent no.4, who is selected in
General Category at Serial No.6 on the post of Revenue
Sub-Inspector (Patwari) at District Tehri Garhwal with a
prayer for mandamus directing the respondent no.1 to
declare the result of the Revenue Sub-Inspector (Patwari)
afresh for the said post on which the petitioner claimed
appointment as against the respondent no.4.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that he has
submitted his application form pursuant to the
advertisement issued by the Commission for the post of
Revenue Sub-Inspector (Patwari/Lekhpal). Petitioner
qualified in the written examination and as per the
scheme of the examination, he was called for the physical
examination and he too qualified in the physical
examination as per the standard fixed by the
Commission.

2
4. It is the contention of learned counsel for the
petitioner that the candidates who are permanent
resident of Hill District requires Hill Certificate to avail the
benefits of the physical specification relaxation given to
the Hill candidates as per the Appendix-3 of the
advertisement. He further contends that respondent no.4,
who admittedly, is a resident of Hill District of
Rudraprayag has submitted a Hill Certificate which was
issued on 29.12.2022 after the last date of the
submission of the application form which is 04.11.2022.
5. To substantiate his argument, learned counsel
for the petitioner has drawn the attention of this Court to
Clause 2 and 5 of the Advertisement, according to which,
the candidates were directed to hold the essential
educational qualification and other eligibility on the last
date of submission of the application form.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Commission
submits that Commission has scrutinised the documents
of the private respondent no.4 and it is only thereafter, he
was selected and recommended for the appointment.
7. I have thoughtfully considered the arguments
advanced on behalf of the petitioner. According to Rule 13
of the Uttarakhand Revenue Sub-Inspectors (Patwari)
Service (First Amendment) Rules, 2015, the candidates of
the Hill District of Uttarakhand have been provided
relaxation in comparison to the candidates belonging to
the plain area qua physical specification towards height
and chest. There is no denial of the fact that respondent
no.4 is a permanent resident of District Rudraprayag,
which is a hill district without any reservation. The
certificate of the private respondent no.4 is annexed as

3
annexure-5 to the writ petition, which reflects that the
said respondent is a resident of Hill District of
Uttarakhand and he is entitled to get the relaxation in the
physical specification of height and chest, and
accordingly, he was selected and recommended for the
appointment. It would hardly make any difference that
this certificate was issued after the last date of
submission of the application form pursuant to the
advertisement issued by the Commission for recruitment.
8. In this view of the matter, this Court finds that
the argument submitted by learned counsel for the
petitioner is hyper-technical and will not come to his help.
It will not make a difference that a candidate is given
certificate of Hill District of Uttarakhand after the last
date of submission of the application form, as there would
not be any change in the height and physical specification
of that candidate.
9. In this view of the matter, I find no force in the
writ petition and the same is dismissed.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 19.09.2023
AK
